final.summary: Recommended: fused. Peak 90th pct core temp 37.96 °C (limit 38.0), tightest margin 0.03 °C, 28% of priority-weighted work done.
reasons: **This plan gets the most done, but leaves almost no safety cushion.** It finishes about 28% of the most important work. The hottest worker is expected to stay just under the 38 °C body-temperature limit, by only a few hundredths of a degree. If the day runs hotter than forecast or someone pushes harder than planned, they could go over. Watch the crew closely and be ready to pull someone into the shade early.
**Dev is new and not used to the heat, so he stays off the heaviest jobs.** Keeping him off the hardest work while it's hot protects him, but it means other crew members carry more of that load.
**Other options trade work done against safety differently:**
**Skill-matching:** Putting skilled workers only on jobs that need their skills gets less done (24%) and runs just as close to the heat limit, so it's not a better choice.
**Cautious:** The safer plan keeps everyone well under the limit (about 37.75 °C) but finishes only 9% of the work.

Hard safety rules:
- Every worker's 90th percentile core temperature must stay below 38.0 °C all shift. Harder work, sun and high WBGT heat people up; 30-min shade rests cool them down.
- Breaks: at most 3 work slots in a row, then a 'rest' slot; at most 2 in a row if any of those slots has WBGT >= 30.0 °C.
- No outdoor tasks during hazards that stop outdoor work. After lightning, outdoor work stays stopped for 30 more minutes.
- Workers who are not acclimatized never do very_heavy tasks when WBGT >= 28.0 °C.
Validity: one entry per slot per worker; off-site workers rest; skills and allowed slots must match.
